[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in content/shell and web_test

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

rewriting to `raw_ptr` was performed.

[TreesInViz] Use indices in EffectTreeLayerListIterator and remove RAW_PTR_EXCLUSION EffectTree* effect_tree_

EffectTreeLayerListIterator processes layer and effect trees that, with
TreesInViz, come from untrusted Mojo input. It held a vector iterator
pointing into LayerTreeImpl's layer list storage, and a separate
RAW_PTR_EXCLUSION EffectTree* next to the RAW_PTR_EXCLUSION
LayerTreeImpl*.

Replace the layer list iterator with a reverse index into the layer
list. The layer is fetched through a new bounds-checked
LayerTreeImpl::LayerAtIndex() on every access. If the layer list changes
during iteration, this now CHECK-fails instead of reading through a
possibly dangling iterator.

Drop the cached EffectTree* and derive the effect tree from
LayerTreeImpl. This only computes an address from the LayerTreeImpl
pointer, so it adds no extra memory load. The iterator now holds a
single pointer, to the tree that owns everything else. It stays
RAW_PTR_EXCLUSION for performance, and the rest of the state is
bounds-checked indices.

No behavior change for valid trees.

[agy][cc] Use offsets in ListContainerHelper and remove RAW_PTR_EXCLUSION InnerList* last_list_

Refactor internal allocator pointers in ListContainerHelper to use
integer offsets instead of raw pointers. Specifically:
- Remove `last_list_` raw pointer in `CharAllocator`, accessing the
  current inner list via `last_list_index_` into `storage_`. This
  avoids dangling pointers when `storage_` reallocates.
- Replace `item_iterator` raw pointer in `PositionInCharAllocator` with
  `item_offset`, eliminating internal raw pointers into allocator
  buffers and deriving `item()` dynamically.

[Contextual Tasks] Clear Lens region on composebox clear

When a region selected in the Lens overlay was attached to the
Contextual Tasks composebox as an "Ask about this image" chip, clearing
the composebox removed the chip but left the region selection drawn on
the overlay. ContextualTasksComposeboxHandler::ClearFiles() reset its
visual selection tokens without notifying the overlay.

ClearFiles() now clears the overlay's region selection when a visual
selection was attached, while keeping the overlay open so the user can
select a new region. Removing the chip directly through DeleteContext()
still closes the overlay, which is intended.

LensComposeboxController now also calls ClearRegionSelection() instead
of ClearAllSelections() when its visual selection chip is removed or its
files are cleared. This clears only the region selection and its
thumbnail, matching the scope of the removed context, rather than every
selection on the overlay.

Adds an interactive UI test that opens the overlay from the Contextual
Tasks composebox Lens button, selects a region, clicks the composebox
clear button, and verifies the region selection is cleared.

[CustomTabs] Deflake CustomTabActivityEphemeralTest#testNonInteractiveOmnibox

CustomTabActivityEphemeralTest.launchCustomTabActivity() called
CustomTabActivityTestRule.startCustomTabActivityWithIntent(), which
invokes waitForFirstFrame() and polls WebContents FrameInfo with a 3000ms
timeout. None of the tests calling launchCustomTabActivity() interact
with DOM elements in WebContents (testNonInteractiveOmnibox only clicks
the Android R.id.title_url_container view in CustomTabToolbar, and
testPopupCreationBlockedAndDoesNotCrashOnClose calls
startCustomTabActivityWithIntent() directly). Under load on CI emulators,
renderer compositor FrameInfo updates can take over 3000ms after page
load, causing waitForFirstFrame() to time out.

Use startCustomTabActivityWithIntentNotWaitingForFirstFrame() in
launchCustomTabActivity(), remove the redundant waitForTabPageLoaded()
call in testNonInteractiveOmnibox(), dismiss the PageInfoController
dialog before tearDown(), and reset IncognitoReauthSettingUtils in
testIncognitoReauthPageNotShown().

Mocking framework classes like View and Activity is discouraged, and
will be disallowed by an Error Prone check. This replaces such mocks
in tests with real instances (e.g. new View(), new FrameLayout(),
Robolectric.buildActivity()) and removes the associated
@SuppressWarnings("DoNotMock").

browser_tests shards on Mac13 Tests currently average ~51m (with P90 at
60.1m), frequently hitting the 60m Swarming execution timeout and
failing with invalid results. Increasing the shard count from 40 to 50
brings the expected average shard runtime down to ~41m.

[glic] Wire up #showError button in GlicOverlayUI and GlicNoWebviewContentsManager

glic_overlay.html already includes the #showError button inside
#errorPanel, but glic_overlay_ui.cc, glic_overlay.mojom,
glic_overlay.ts, and GlicNoWebviewContentsManager never wired up
showErrorAllowed or a click handler. When a load fails or times out to
ErrorPanelType::kError in GlicNoWebview mode, internal/dev users could
not view the underlying guest WebContents to inspect the error or bypass
a block page.

- Add OnShowErrorClicked() to GlicOverlayPageHandler in
  glic_overlay.mojom.
- Populate showErrorAllowed on GlicOverlayUI's WebUIDataSource when the
  primary account is Google-internal, --glic-dev is passed, or
  prefs::kGlicShowErrorAllowed is enabled.
- Unhide #showError in glic_overlay.ts when showErrorAllowed is true and
  forward clicks to onShowErrorClicked().
- Implement OverlayContentsManager::OnShowErrorClicked() to clear the
  overlay error, set is_guest_error_ = true, and swap display state to
  guest_contents() while keeping ShouldReloadOnShow() true.

with their dead comments; 30 are still needed.

  web_app_toolbar_button_container_impl, bookmarks:impl,
  bookmarks/saved_tab_groups:impl, sharing_hub:impl,
  tabs/shared:impl, tabs/dragging:impl.

- The remaining 16 are genuinely needed, but their comments listed
  far more headers than actually remain blocking (e.g.
  location_bar:impl's comment named 18 headers; only
  browser_tabstrip.h still is one). Every one of the 16 now reduces
  to headers from just 4 remaining monolithic files:
  browser_tabstrip.h, base_tab_strip_region_view.h,
  horizontal_tab_strip_region_view.h, and
  vertical_tab_strip_region_view.h. Comments are rewritten in a
  single normalized format:
  "TODO(crbug.com/<NUM>): Remove this circular dependency when the
  following header(s) get(s) componentized:" + a bullet list.

Verified with `gn gen --check` on desktop, ChromeOS, and Android, plus
real autoninja compiles of chrome/browser/ui:ui and all 16 remaining
consumer targets on desktop and ChromeOS.

Android: Replace View / Activity mocks with real objects (simple-1)

Mocking framework classes like View and Activity is discouraged, and
will be disallowed by an Error Prone check. This fixes tests where the
mocked View / Activity was used only as an opaque object (or had no
meaningful stubs), replacing them with real instances (new View(),
new FrameLayout(), Robolectric.buildActivity()), and removes the
associated @SuppressWarnings("DoNotMock").

[PublicTransit] Handle leftover CTS MockIme in SoftKeyboardCondition

On shared Swarming physical devices, a prior Android CTS test can leave
Settings.Secure.DEFAULT_INPUT_METHOD set to
com.android.cts.mockime/com.android.cts.mockime.MockIme without an
active MockImeSession. When a Public Transit test (such as
OmniboxDisplayStatePTTest or PublicTransitLeakTest#omniboxTest) calls
CtaPageStation.openOmnibox(), MockIme.onCreate() immediately throws
IllegalStateException ('Settings file is not found. Make sure
MockImeSession.create() is used to launch Mock IME') and crashes before
any soft keyboard window is shown.

Because CtaPageStation.openOmnibox() only enters SoftKeyboardFacility in
order to immediately close the soft keyboard via softKeyboard.close(),
teach SoftKeyboardCondition.determineIfSoftKeyboardShouldShow() to treat
a leftover com.android.cts.mockime default input method as not expected
to show a soft keyboard.

[WebApps] Add SECURITY.md for desktop web apps and IWAs

Add a canonical SECURITY.md in //components/webapps/ following the
format and requirements in //docs/security/security_md_guidelines.md and
referencing //docs/security/security-for-agents.md. The document defines
the security boundaries, trust assumptions, threat model, in-scope
vulnerabilities, and explicit non-bugs for desktop Progressive Web Apps
(PWAs) and Isolated Web Apps (IWAs).

Because security triage tooling resolves only the nearest ancestor
SECURITY.md, add pointer and summary stubs in
//chrome/browser/web_applications/ and //chrome/browser/webapps/ that
summarize core invariants and point to the corresponding SECURITY.md
files.

[Extensions] Enable navigator.clipboard in extension service workers

Turns on the runtime flag for extension processes. Adds
IsClipboardAllowedForServiceWorker, which gates
ServiceWorkerHost::BindClipboardHost on the worker's origin, so an
ineligible worker never gets a ClipboardHost.

ServiceWorkerClipboardContext::CanWrite asks the existing
AllowWorkerWriteToClipboard per call, so revoking clipboardWrite takes
effect on a running worker. Reads stay unsupported.

Adds apitests for a worker that writes and one without the permission.

[SCWW] Add LaunchOnStartupEnabled enterprise policy

Adds a Windows-only LaunchOnStartupEnabled policy for the "Start
Chrome with Windows" setting (launch_on_login.foreground.enabled):

- Enabled: Chrome launches and opens a browser window at Windows
  sign-in. Users can't change the setting.
- Disabled: Chrome doesn't launch at sign-in. Users can't change the
  setting.
- Unset: users decide.

The policy can also be set as recommended, in which case users can
still change the setting. The settings toggle shows the enterprise
indicator, and is locked when the policy is mandatory.

The Start Chrome with Windows infobar is not shown when the setting is
managed or recommended by policy. Since the pref observer also fires
on policy changes, Startup.Launch.Foreground.PreferenceChanged is now
only recorded for user-set values.

The policy takes effect only while the LaunchOnStartup feature is
enabled, so the feature flag remains a kill switch.

iOS tests assert that name. histograms.xml, however, registered it as

unregistered.

[WebAudio] Refactor and optimize AudioParam sizing in AudioWorklet

AudioWorkletProcessor::Process previously scanned all 128 float elements
in ParamValueMapMatchesToParamsObject and CloneParamValueMapToObject on
every render quantum to check whether an AudioParam had constant values.
Meanwhile, AudioWorkletHandler always passed full 128-element buffers
regardless of automation rate or sample accuracy.

This CL moves the sizing logic into AudioWorkletHandler with zero
audio-thread heap allocations:
- Pre-allocate backing AudioFloatArray buffers (`param_buffers_`) to
  RenderQuantumFrames() on the main thread and expose active
  `base::span<const float>` views in `param_value_map_`.
- Share SIMD-accelerated `audio_utilities::HasConstantValues()` between
  BiquadFilterHandler and AudioWorkletHandler to slice constant or
  k-rate parameter spans to length 1 and varying sample-accurate a-rate
  spans to `frames_to_process`.
- Remove the redundant O(N) per-quantum loops in AudioWorkletProcessor
  and use `param_values.size()` directly.
- Add unit tests covering `AudioWorkletProcessor::Process` size
  transitions and `AudioWorkletHandler::Process` parameter sizing.

Don't match IWAs via scope extensions in notification attribution

An https origin in installed IWA's validated scope extensions resolved
to the IWA origin, letting the origin borrow the IWA's name, icon and
shelf badge in notification UI.

To fix that, exclude the scope extended IWA origins when performing
WebApp look ups for notification attribution.

Additionally, WebAppRegistrar::FindBestAppWithUrlInScope now ignores
IWA scope extensions by default (callers that need them opt in), its
two overloads are merged into one, and the :isolated_web_app_test GN
target is extracted.

Original change's description:
> [TTC] Add VoiceFocusedContentsTracker with a Desktop implementation
>
> Adds VoiceFocusedContentsTracker, which reports the active tab of
> the active browser window and notifies observers when it changes.
>
> The tracker binds to the profile's active browser window when created,
> or to the first one activated afterwards if there is none. :
>   - Switching tabs within the bound window changes the active tab.
>   - Activating a different window replaces the bound window.
>   - Closing the bound window sets the bound browser to the last
>   active browser on the browser collection observation.
>
> VoiceFocusedContentsTracker is a platform-agnostic base class; each
> platform provides a subclass and defines VFCT::Create(). This CL
> adds VoiceFocusedContentsTrackerDesktop, built on
> ProfileBrowserCollection and
> BrowserWindowInterface::RegisterActiveTabDidChange(). The Android
> implementation follows in a separate CL.

Reland "Prevent Glic experimental triggering handler cleanup on self-superseded invocations."

This is a reland of commit 39ef7e499af513a02219c1d36d91ecccbf8e8443

PS1 is the original commit. The fix is very simple,
we just need to check the pending ids only when the
error is superseded.


Original change's description:
> Prevent Glic experimental triggering handler cleanup on self-superseded invocations.
>
> Experimental triggering updates handlers are shared per context id, so a
> continuation request invokes on the same handler that owns the in-flight
> invocation it supersedes. GlicInvokeHandler::OnError() posts the
> kSuperseded error asynchronously, so the handler previously tore itself
> down (and stopped delivering updates) on the next task, even though the
> continuation invocation was still in flight and waiting for updates.
>
> Track the set of in-flight invocation IDs (`pending_invoke_ids_`) on
> ExperimentalTriggeringUpdatesHandler, removing each ID in
> OnInvokeSuccess() and OnInvokeError(), and ignore errors while another
> invocation started by the same handler remains in flight.
>

Screen readers like VoiceOver were getting confused about what text to
read because other sources like the input text field or the browser's
location bar were also driving narration. With this change, the full
webui omnibox popup owns its narration and uses match a11y text when
appropriate.

first account in the cookie jar rather than the primary account. Update

ios: Support iPhone Duo simulator rotation and sequential testing

On the iPhone Duo simulator, standard XCUIDevice.setOrientation
calls do not drive device orientation transitions in locationd or
SpringBoard. Instead, the simulator requires vendor-defined HID
events.

This change:
- Swizzles -[EarlGreyImpl rotateInterfaceToOrientation:error:] on
  the Duo simulator to route rotation requests through
  ChromeEarlGrey's simulated Duo orientation HID helper.
- Restores orientation to Portrait before closing the hinge during
  teardown and setup, preventing SpringBoard from deferring
  orientation updates on the cover display.
- Forces clones=1 for iPhone Duo in SimulatorTestRunner and
  SimulatorParallelTestRunner because host-wide HID events have no
  simulator isolation and cross-talk across parallel workers.

[cbor] Fix invalid UTF-8 in CBOR values in-place

Add mutable GetArray() and GetMap() accessors to cbor::Value and update
device::FixInvalidUTF8() to mutate INVALID_UTF8 leaf nodes in-place,
saving both time and memory:

- Eliminates the separate ContainsInvalidUTF8() pre-pass, reducing two
  tree traversals to a single pass when invalid UTF-8 is present.
- Eliminates the implicit third tree traversal required to destroy the
  input value when invalid UTF-8 was present.
- Avoids cloning every leaf value and map key in the CBOR structure and
  allocating new arrays and maps, the latter of which also required
  pointless binary-searching in the underlying flat_map during the
  emplace calls even though the keys were guaranteed to be inserted in
  sorted order.
- Moves the repaired std::string into cbor::Value instead of copying it.

This contains no intentional observable behavioral changes.

tracing: Don't always wait for the full timeout in shmem test

`TraceStartupSharedMemoryTest.PassSharedMemoryRegion` passes a
`base::WaitableEvent` to the IO-thread task that launches the child
process, but the task never signals it. The test thread therefore
always sleeps for the full `TestTimeouts::action_timeout()` (10s),
even though the child exits in well under a second on desktop.

Worse, when the child does time out, the task's `EXPECT`s fire after
the test has already returned and are reported against whichever test
runs next. On Android this shows up as `SnooperNodeTest` failures.

Signal the event once the child has exited, and wait for it without a
timeout. The task's own wait on the child is already bounded by
`action_timeout()`, and an untimed wait guarantees `wait` outlives the
task.

On Android the child crashes before running its test body, so the test
has never passed there. Now that the failure is reported correctly,
disable it on Android until that is fixed.

Locally on Linux this takes the test from 10001 ms to ~330 ms.

[🌺] Revert "[Omnibox] Replace mocked Views in HeaderDecorationUnitTest"

This reverts commit 49991540bb0c653d036b9b121af41b8388356691.

Reason for revert: consistently fails android-internal-desktop-x64-rel.

HeaderDecorationUnitTest#testGetItemOffsets_withHeader has failed in
8/25 recent builds of android-internal-desktop-x64-rel, every attempt in
every one of them. This is not flake: it reproduces on every run, so it
blocks the CQ for every unrelated CL that touches this suite. The
regression appears at refs/heads/main@{#1708180}.

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/try/android-internal-desktop-x64-rel/27906

Replacing mocked RecyclerView with TestRecyclerView in
HeaderDecorationUnitTest calls mRecyclerView.addView(...) in setUp()
(HeaderDecorationUnitTest.java:123) without a LayoutManager set on
TestRecyclerView, throwing java.lang.IllegalStateException: RecyclerView
has no LayoutManager across all 8 parameterized tests.

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

Original change's description:

Ignore <source> child element insertion when srcObject is present

Per the WHATWG HTML specification, child <source> elements are only
evaluated if the media element has neither an assigned media provider
object (srcObject) nor a src attribute.

Prior to this CL, HTMLMediaElement::SourceWasAdded() only checked
FastHasAttribute(srcAttr), completely omitting the check for srcObject.

interferes with keyboard users and ATs. This patch allows selection to

text inside the input.

Fix WindowAndroid UAF in BlurTransitionAnimationManager

BlurTransitionAnimationManager observes WindowAndroid while animating
but was never told when its view was detached from the window. During
graceful tab shutdown, TabWebContentsDestroyer keeps the WebContents
alive after the tab is detached; if the WindowAndroid is destroyed in
the meantime, ~BlurTransitionAnimationManager later calls
RemoveObserver() on freed memory.

Observe the WebContents' ViewAndroid and abort the transition and drop
the window observation on OnDetachedFromWindow() and
OnViewAndroidDestroyed(). DestroyLayer() now always resets the window
observation.

Avoid creating the shared D-Bus session bus in DynamicLauncherPortal

DynamicLauncherPortal checked whether it was using the shared session
bus by comparing its bus with dbus_thread_linux::GetSharedSessionBus(),
which creates the shared bus if it doesn't exist yet. When a custom bus
was passed in (as in unit tests), this created a shared bus bound to the
test's task environment that outlived the test. A later test in the
same process that shuts down the shared bus (e.g. via
RenderViewHostTestHarness::TearDown()) then crashed with a dangling
raw_ptr, e.g. when EyeDropperPortalTest ran after
DynamicLauncherPortalTest.

Determine whether the shared bus is used at construction instead.

- Mark 68 multi-case wdspec tests as [ Slow ] in SlowTests and update
  corresponding Android [ Timeout ] entries in TestExpectations to
  [ Skip Timeout ].

52d9093f8ed9a7410c23b8720d3b57af4ddc13cf [ diff ] 
fontconfig: Unblock C/C++ compilation from Rust bindgen actions

Previously, `component("fontconfig")` included `:fontconfig_fontations_ffi`
directly in its `deps`. Because `:fontconfig_fontations_ffi` depends on
`rust_bindgen("fcint_h_bindgen")` and `rust_bindgen("fontconfig_h_bindgen")`,
GN propagated the bindgen action outputs into `fontconfig.harddeps`.

As a result, all fontconfig C files (such as `fcatomic.c` and `fccfg.c`) as
well as downstream C/C++ compile steps depending on `//third_party/fontconfig`
were blocked waiting for the Rust bindgen actions and Rust sysroot (`libstd`)
to complete (~68 seconds in build traces), delaying up to 5,477 compile steps.

However, fontconfig's C implementation only references the Rust symbol via
an extern declaration (`extern int add_patterns_to_fontset(...)` in
`fcfontations.c`) and does not include any generated bindings.

Split the fontconfig C compilation into a `source_set("fontconfig_sources")`
without the Rust dependency, and have `component("fontconfig")` depend on
`:fontconfig_sources` and `:fontconfig_fontations_ffi`. This removes the
bindgen action from C harddeps, allowing fontconfig C sources and downstream
C++ targets to compile immediately at the start of the build.

[audio] Allow enabling audio processing in CreateInputDevice

When capturing audio, callers sometimes need Chrome's audio service to
automatically remove echo, filter out background noise, or adjust
microphone volume (gain control).

What this CL does:
1. Adds an optional AudioProcessingSettings parameter to
   CreateInputDevice so callers can request software processing when
   starting microphone capture.
2. Forwards these settings through InputIPC to the Audio Service.
3. Keeps all existing callers working without changes (defaults to no
   software processing).

Consolidate vertical layout updates (sheet translation Y, handlebar top
margin, content container height, content bottom padding, background

BottomSheetMediator#updateVerticalLayout() invoked from

61ef27611dc69f16b6fe899c8b90a80330ac88df [ diff ] 
[PWA] Fix origin association backfill landing in the future

When an app has no origin_association_last_validation_check_time, the
command backfills one. The comment says to randomize it "in the past to
ensure no network fetch spikes", but the code computed
Now() + delta + base::Days(1), which is 1-2 days in the future.

Combined with the 24h throttle below, that defers the first real
revalidation to Now() + delta + 2 days -- 2 to 3 days out, rather than
the intended 0 to 1. A revoked scope extension therefore stays trusted
about two days longer than the throttle promises, on every launch path,
for any app whose timestamp is unset.

- base::Days(1) is what the surrounding code describes: the stored time
lands in [now - 1 day, now], and the throttle turns that into a first
fetch at a uniformly random point within 24 hours, which is what spreads
the load.

The existing test asserted the bug rather than the intent:

  // The time should be within the last 10 days.
  EXPECT_GE(*app->origin_association_last_validation_check_time(),
            clock().Now());

The comment says the past; the assertion required the future. Assert both
bounds instead, so the offset cannot silently flip sign again, and add
NotThrottledWithinADayOfBackfill to cover the property that actually
matters -- that a backfilled app becomes eligible within a day. Both tests
fail against the previous arithmetic.

The stray "10 days" predates the throttle being 24h and is dropped.

In ResourceMultiBufferDataProvider::DidReceiveResponse(), check a
WeakPtr across old_url_data->RedirectTo(destination_url_data).

reset reader_ and delete the active ResourceMultiBufferDataProvider when
the redirect destination already has sufficient cached data and
cancel_on_defer_ is set.

parent
d339c5586b76c184604020e9e5337bb9dcf40387 [ diff ] 
[CRD Linux] Terminate the logind session when desktop-session exits

pam_systemd moves the session processes started by
chrome-remote-desktop-x11-session@.service into the logind session
scope, so KillMode doesn't cover them, and cleanup() only kills
desktop-session's direct children. Daemonized processes, such as XDG
autostart apps, keep running after desktop-session exits. With the
default KillUserProcesses=no, logind then leaves the session in the
"closing" state indefinitely, and `loginctl terminate-session` becomes
a no-op.

Explicitly terminate the logind session via Session.Terminate after
cleanup(), while the session is still active, so that logind stops the
session scope. This is similar to how GDM's gnome-headless-session
terminates its sessions. SIGTERM and SIGHUP are ignored right before
the call, since terminating the session also signals desktop-session
itself, which would otherwise interrupt the atexit handlers and could
drop RELAUNCH_EXIT_CODE. The session is only terminated if its PAM
service is chrome-remote-desktop and this process is its leader, so
running the script manually from another session doesn't log the user
out. Each D-Bus call has a short timeout, so that a hung logind can't
delay the exit past TimeoutStopSec.

Also fix the misleading KillMode comment in the unit file.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in ash/wm/desks

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`) throughout the `ash/wm/desks` module.
This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr safety initiative to protect
against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

rewriting to `raw_ptr` was performed.

[Autofill] Remove LogEventCountsUMAMetric to fix shutdown hang

Unconditionally running LogEventCountsUMAMetric() for every cached form
during ~BrowserAutofillManager() causes iOS watchdog timeouts
(0x8BADF00D) when closing many realized WebStates. Removes
LogEventCountsUMAMetric() as it is no longer needed since
kMaxLogEventsPerField was introduced.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAMS=Patterned histogram Autofill.LogEvent.{LogEventTypes} was removed in 2026/09 as it caused shutdown hangs and is no longer needed.

Support vertical padding in MenuItemBackground

Adds top_padding and bottom_padding fields to MenuItemBackground to
allow extra background-colored space above and below a menu item.

Child views, icons, text, and container margins are adjusted so that
content remains centered within the inner row. Selection and highlight
painting are updated so the highlight covers only the row, excluding the
padding, and clips to the background's rounded corners when applicable.

Reland "[A11y] Enable TWCC events for Form Control and Widget Tests"

This is a reland of commit 7c3d7bb1201923211ed65e147b7646dd697f1d9b

Original change's description:
> [A11y] Enable TWCC events for Form Control and Widget Tests
>
> This is Batch 2 of 6 in the project to enable
> TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED (TWCC) events across Android accessibility
> event dump tests.
>
> In this CL:
>     - Pass shouldFilterTrivialEvents=false for 46 form control and widget tests (buttons, checkboxes, comboboxes, menulists, sliders, range inputs, spinbuttons, and listboxes)
>     - Update the corresponding 46 expectation files to reflect the full TWCC event stream.
>
> Change-Id: I0393eae053a2e44a918d83d9409d303821c0f4dd
> Bug: 414363686
> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8292012
> Reviewed-by: Aeryn Moss <aerynm@google.com>
> Reviewed-by: Lucas Radaelli <lucasradaelli@google.com>
> Commit-Queue: Kavya Mehta <kavyamehta@google.com>
> Reviewed-by: Kyra Seevers <kyraseevers@chromium.org>
> Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/main@{#1706703}

Reason for reland:
- test_ariaComboboxFocus emits TWCC events in a different order
  depending on the Android version/form factor (Android 13 vs. Android
  15 tablet), so a single expectation file cannot pass on all bots. It is
  removed from this batch and keeps trivial-event filtering with its
  original expectation.

[iOS][TTC] Implement TTCConversation

Introduces TTCConversation to manage audio and conversation state for
TalkToChrome on iOS:
- Implements 3-state machine (kStopped, kListening, kTalking)
- Integrates with TTCAudioController for capture and playback
- Disallows client-side barge-in during assistant playback (Phase 1)
- Wires TTCSessionController to own and drive TTCConversation
- Adds unit test coverage for state transitions, chunks, and energy

d5765c8df9354f5848a2f9d503a4d1c2511b4004 [ diff ] 
gpu: Zero-initialize the offscreen backbuffer in ResizeOffscreenFramebuffer

The validating decoder allocates the offscreen target color texture with
uninitialized storage and relies on a native glClear to initialize it.
On drivers with the gl_clear_broken workaround, glClear is unreliable,
and the workaround's draw-based clear (ClearFramebufferForWorkaround)
can't be used here because ResizeOffscreenFramebuffer runs from
Initialize() before clear_framebuffer_blit_ is created. Since
AllocateStorage() marks the level as fully cleared, the texture is never
lazily cleared afterwards, so its contents could be left as recycled
GPU memory.

Upload zeros when allocating the storage so the backbuffer contents are
defined regardless of glClear behavior. This is a one-time allocation
at context initialization, so the cost is negligible.

Rework OverflowableToolbarActionContainerMixin overflow logic.

The old overflow logic grouped dividers with the element immediately to
their left. This worked, as long as elements were in strict priority
order (right highest, left lowest), including all `preventOverflow`
elements being to the right of all non-preventOverflow elements.

Unfortunately, those assumptions don't actually hold, so this CL
switches to a new algorithm:

1) In setToMinWidth(), we walk through the action elements from left to
right, showing only elements with `preventOverflow` set, and hiding all
others. For divider elements, we show them if we've seen any
`preventOverflow` element since the last divider.
2) In expandUpToPreferredWidth(), we use basically the same algorithm
as before, but modified to skip over already-visible dividers, which
might not have an already-visible action immediately to their left.

This gives us slightly modified effective behavior: All actions between
{a divider | start of the array Array} and a divider are logically
grouped together, and if we show any of them, then the divider on their
right will be shown. We don't implement it like that because in
expandUpToPreferredWidth(), we need to consider any hidden divider
at the same time as the action immediately to its left.

This CL doesn't affect any observable behavior, because the one
consumer of OverflowableToolbarActionContainerMixin currently never
has a `preventOverflow` element to the left of any
non-`preventOverflow` elements, but that is going to change in a
followup CL.

parent
8b323a0f030da546190a7b013e18254f1b4612f1 [ diff ] 
blink: Isolate font_resource.cc to unblock core and downstream harddeps

In component('core'), loader/resource/font_resource.cc is the only
non-test translation unit that includes ift_patcher.h from
//third_party/blink/renderer/platform:font_rust_headers.

Having component('core') depend directly on :font_rust_headers adds
Crubit-generated font headers (font_format.h and ift_patcher_rs.h) to
core.harddeps, which propagates transitively through blink and content
to 4,102 targets and blocks 14,187 C++ compilation steps until Crubit
standard library and font bindings finish generating (~127s on a cold
build).

Split loader/resource/font_resource.h into
blink_core_sources('font_resource_header') and
loader/resource/font_resource.cc into blink_core_sources('font_resource')
with public = [] so that :font_rust_headers harddeps remain scoped to
font_resource.cc alone without adding any circular include exceptions
(reducing reachable .harddeps targets from 4,102 to 13).

Like :core_hot, these targets use the blink_core_sources template so that
they inherit core's common configs and deps from core.gni instead of
duplicating them. blink_core_sources now always creates a source_set for
header-only targets, since an empty static_library fails to be created
with lld-link /lib on Windows non-component builds.

blink: Decouple media/capture:video_capture dependency from mojom_platform

//third_party/blink/public/mojom:mojom_platform depended on
//media/capture/mojom:video_capture in public_deps, but none of the
mojom files in mojom_platform import video_capture.mojom (they only
import video_capture_types.mojom).

The C++ code in blink/renderer/platform (video_capture_impl.h and
tests) that interacts with VideoCaptureHost imports
video_capture.mojom-blink.h. By exposing video_capture_blink in
component("platform") public_deps (consistent with other mojom
blink bindings in platform), tests and consumers can use the
interfaces exported by blink_platform.dll without adding
video_capture_blink to static unit test source sets.

This removes the serial dependency between video_capture and
mojom_platform on the critical path, and avoids duplicate symbol
linker errors in Windows component builds.

ManagedConfigurationAPI origin configurations and installed web app
metadata from WebAppRegistrar, formatting them as managed configuration
sections for chrome://policy and dynamically updating when web apps are
installed/uninstalled or managed configurations change.

[WebNN] Fix CoreML build by moving GetContextProperties to ContextImplCoreml

CL 8032700 included services/webnn/coreml/graph_builder_coreml.h in
webnn_context_provider_impl.cc to call GraphBuilderCoreml::GetContextProperties().
However, webnn_context_provider_impl.cc is part of webnn_service_base,
which does not depend on //third_party/coremltools:modelformat_proto.
Because graph_builder_coreml.h includes MIL.pb.h, remote execution builds
on Mac (such as 'Libfuzzer Upload Mac ASan') fail with:
fatal error: 'third_party/coremltools/mlmodel/format/MIL.pb.h' file not found

Expose static ContextProperties GetContextProperties() on ContextImplCoreml
instead (analogous to ContextImplOrt::GetContextProperties), which avoids
including graph_builder_coreml.h in webnn_context_provider_impl.cc.

[Passwords] Mock elapsed timer in auth time test

PasswordsPrivateDelegateImplMockTaskEnvironmentTest.AuthenticationTimeMetric
was migrated from a unit test (with TimeSource::MOCK_TIME) to a browser
test in https://crrev.com/c/7764703 and updated to assert that
PasswordManager.Settings.AuthenticationTime2 falls in Bucket 0
(base::Seconds(0), which requires real wall-clock time to be under
10ms).

On slower sanitizer bots such as Linux Chromium OS ASan LSan Tests (1)
or under CPU contention, the synchronous call between
TimeCallbackMediumTimes() and the mock AuthenticateWithMessage callback
frequently takes 10-26ms, causing the sample to land in Bucket 10 or 25
and failing the test.

Install base::ScopedMockElapsedTimersForTest in the test so that
base::ElapsedTimer::Elapsed() deterministically returns kMockElapsedTime
regardless of real wall-clock execution time.

[ash] login/signin: drop the chrome/browser/signin dependency

The whole of chrome/browser/ash/login/signin was allowed to include
chrome/browser/signin because five non-factory files looked their
//chrome dependencies up themselves.

Pass signin::IdentityManager in through the constructor of
OAuth2LoginManager, SigninErrorNotifier, TokenHandleService and
AuthErrorObserver, and SigninErrorController into AuthErrorObserver;
their factories already DependsOn() those, except for the two that now
also DependsOn(IdentityManagerFactory). OAuth2LoginManager's use of
AccountIdFromAccountInfo() is replaced by the KnownUser lookup that
helper performs on ChromeOS.

AccountReconcilor is deliberately left as a lazy lookup: injecting it
would create the reconcilor, and start a reconcile cycle, as soon as
OAuth2LoginManager is built.

What remains is scoped to the factories, to
legacy_token_handle_fetcher.cc (whose shutdown-notifier factory lives in
the same file) and to tests.

#ai-assisted

[WebMCP] Remove origin-keyed agent cluster requirement

Previously, document.modelContext's registerTool(), getTools() and
executeTool() rejected with a SecurityError, and declarative tools were
silently not registered, when the document was not in an origin-keyed
agent cluster (i.e. when document.domain could be used). The spec no
longer has this requirement, so remove the check.

This also removes the tests that asserted the old behavior, including
the --disable-web-security exception test, which is now moot.

Spec PR: https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/pull/330

Wed Sep 30 16:53:12 2026
tree
d6f8f9738a45d819cf2b16d88fc25dd7eb87d28b
parent
a68f71bd03a1189339ca322b30d1621e3c4f0f7e [ diff ] 
[EVP] Require a bare host name in the DNS iss= record

The spec says the DNS delegation record carries `iss=` followed by the
issuer's host name (§3.1), and that the issuer identifier is "https://"
followed by that host, with no port, path or trailing slash, compared
byte-for-byte (§3.2):
https://dickhardt.github.io/email-verification/draft-hardt-email-verification.html#name-dns-delegation
https://dickhardt.github.io/email-verification/draft-hardt-email-verification.html#name-issuer-identifier

Chromium only checked that the value was non-empty and then passed it
through GURL, which silently normalized it: a port was kept in the
issuer identifier, a path was dropped, uppercase was lowercased, and a
query, fragment or userinfo was carried into the
.well-known/email-verification URL.

Now the record is rejected with kDnsInvalidRecord unless its value is
already exactly a canonical host. Existing issuers publish bare hosts
(e.g. iss=accounts.google.com) and are unaffected.

[🌷] Deflake DevToolsExtensionTest.CantInspectRemoteNewTabPage

DevToolsExtensionTest.CantInspectRemoteNewTabPage added a custom
TemplateURL and set it as the user-selected default search provider
without waiting for TemplateURLService to finish loading from
WebDataService. When OnWebDataServiceRequestDone() completed
asynchronously on the UI thread, SetTemplateURLs() replaced
template_urls_ in memory, causing the custom New Tab Page URL to not be
recognized as a restricted NTP and allowing the DevTools extension to
inspect it.

Wait for TemplateURLService to load via
search_test_utils::WaitForTemplateURLServiceToLoad() before adding the
custom TemplateURL.

5915a6eb670d9b2530c49d58f425b173f685d013 [ diff ] 
[TabModel] Consolidate onTabGroup* callbacks onto TabGroupObserver

TabModelObserver previously duplicated tab group lifecycle callbacks
(onTabGroupCreated, onTabGroupRemoving, onTabGroupMoved, and
onTabGroupVisualsChanged) alongside TabGroupObserver solely so
TabModelObserverJniBridge could forward group events to native
observers. This forced TabCollectionTabModelImpl to iterate all
registered TabModelObservers on every tab group creation, move, visual
update, and removal even though TabModelObserverJniBridge was the only
consumer.

Have TabModelObserverJniBridge implement TabGroupObserver directly, move
onTabGroupVisualsChanged to TabGroupObserver, and remove the duplicate
callbacks and observer loops from TabModelObserver and
TabCollectionTabModelImpl. Routing willRemoveTabGroup through
TabModelObserverJniBridge also ensures native observers receive
OnTabGroupRemoving when a tab group is dissolved via ungrouping,
merging, or group creation undo.

[Extensions] Fix ScriptInjectionTracker desync for RequestContentScript

Previously, RequestContentScript::InstructRenderProcessToInject() used
PermissionsData::CanAccessPage() to check if an extension could inject a
declarative content script into a frame. Because CanAccessPage() returns
true even when host permissions are withheld, the browser invoked
ScriptInjectionTracker::WillExecuteCode() prematurely before sending
ExecuteDeclarativeScript() to the renderer. In the renderer,
ScriptInjection::TryToInject() detected that permissions were withheld
and deferred execution. This caused the browser and renderer states to
desynchronize: the browser erroneously considered the renderer process
as having executed the extension's content script even though no script
ran.

With this change, the browser does not update ScriptInjectionTracker
when page access is withheld during declarative content script
evaluation. Instead, the renderer defers the script and requests
permission via ExtensionActionRunner. Once the user explicitly grants
permission on the tab, the deferred script executes in the renderer and
ScriptInjectionTracker is updated so browser and renderer states remain
synchronized.

We update RequestContentScript::InstructRenderProcessToInject() to query
PermissionsData::GetPageAccess() directly and only call
ScriptInjectionTracker::WillExecuteCode() when access is kAllowed. We
also add mojom::InjectionType::kDeclarativeScript, which
UserScriptInjector reports for RequestContentScript scripts, and have
ExtensionActionRunner gate it on PermissionsData::GetPageAccess() so
withheld requests are queued. ExtensionActionRunner already notifies
ScriptInjectionTracker before permitting pending scripts to execute.

Enable Skia Graphite on Windows in FormControlsBrowserTest

On Windows, the baseline images in content/test/data/forms/ were
rebaselined with Skia Graphite enabled via
fieldtrial_testing_config.json (which enables SkiaGraphite and
SkiaGraphiteWinIntel on Windows).

In branded builds where fieldtrial_testing_config.json is disabled,
content_browsertests falls back to Skia Ganesh, which renders the
<textarea> rounded corners and diagonal resize grip lines without
antialiasing and causes FormControlsBrowserTest.Textarea to exceed the
average absolute error limit (13.91 vs 12.0).

Explicitly enable features::kSkiaGraphite and
features::kSkiaGraphiteWinIntel in FormControlsBrowserTest on Windows so
both branded and unbranded builds use the same Skia backend as the
Windows baselines.

[WebUI Toolbar] Align home button plain-text drop behavior on macOS

Aligns drag-and-drop on the WebUI toolbar home button with the native
Views HomeButton on macOS.

The native HomeButton only accepts drops that carry a URL. On macOS,
ui::clipboard_util::URLsAndTitlesFromPasteboard() already synthesizes a
URL from URL-like plain text, so such drags reach the WebUI toolbar as
`text/uri-list` and are routed to OnHomeButtonDropUrl(). A drop that is
still `text/plain` only therefore carries no URL, and the native button
ignores it regardless of where the drag started.

WebUIHomeControl::ShouldHandleDropText() now returns false on macOS for
every `text/plain`-only drop, and consumes the pending drag origin state
so it does not leak into later navigations.

[Settings] Ignore Chrome sign-in choice for an unknown account

PeopleHandler::HandleSetChromeSigninUserChoice() looks up the account
by the email sent from the settings page. The page is refreshed when the
signed-in accounts change (e.g. OnPrimaryAccountChanged() on sign-out),
but the request is asynchronous and can race with the account being
removed, and the email is renderer-provided. When the lookup fails it
returns an empty AccountInfo, and the handler went on to use an empty
GaiaId:
- SetChromeSigninInterceptionUserChoice() stored the choice under an
  empty key in "signin.accounts_metadata_dict", and
- for kDoNotSignin, ClearChromeSigninInterceptionLastBubbleDeclineTime()
  hit CHECK(!gaia_id.empty()) in SigninPrefs::ClearPref() and crashed
  the browser.

Return early when the account is not found, before any pref write or
histogram recording.

Remove SelectiveClipboardFormatRead

Remove an earlier version of the selective clipboard format feature that
was eventually superseded by the version shipped in [1], which makes
ClipboardItem.getType() "lazy" rather than requiring callers to pass a
list of the formats they'll want.

This is basically a revert of [2] and [3], including changing the name
of the ClipboardReadOptions dict back to ClipboardUnsanitizedFormats so
that the Chromium IDL again matches the spec [4].

[1] https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7862426
[2] https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6870271
[3] https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6915376
[4] https://w3c.github.io/clipboard-apis/#clipboard-interface

[browser_actuator] Add end-to-end FCM to StartSessionAck test

Add BrowserActuatorFcmIntegrationTest in
chrome/browser/sharing/browser_actuator/browser_actuator_message_handler_unittest.cc to verify the end-to-end component flow when an FCM message
arrives.

Wires SharingFCMHandler, BrowserActuatorMessageHandler, and
BrowserActuatorServiceFactory on a TestingProfile connected to
FakeProtoStreamServer, verifying that receiving an FCM SharingMessage
with StartSession (or GlicExperimentalTriggering) starts the downstream
transport channel, sends the upstream StartSessionAck (or feature
reply), records the session in SessionStreamRecorderFactory, and tears
down the session on downstream CloseSession.

[STTS] Mark entry opened before loading URL in iOS notification client

In SendTabPushNotificationClient::HandleNotificationInteraction,
openURLInNewTab: creates an active WebState and inserts it into
WebStateList, synchronously triggering WebStateListDidChange in
SendTabToSelfBrowserAgent. If the entry is not yet marked opened in the
model, the browser agent treats it as unopened and opens a duplicate
background tab while emitting a duplicate outcome sample.

Marking the entry opened and activated in the model before dispatching
openURLInNewTab: prevents this reentrancy issue.

parent
4463ee8c39a9c9d31c5c9c7a514924bba1303139 [ diff ] 
[rust] Read `src/stage0` from the local Rust checkout, not Gitiles.

`FetchBetaPackage` fetched `src/stage0` from Gitiles.  Since about
2026-09-26, Gitiles returns HTTP 503 for most unauthenticated
requests (https://crbug.com/567198974).  This breaks all
`*_upload_rust` bots.

This CL reads the local `src/stage0` file instead.  All callers check
out Rust first, or use an existing checkout (`--skip-checkout`).  This
CL adds no new source of trust:
- The old code read the same file, at the same commit, from the same
  GoB repo (through Gitiles instead of git).
- `VerifyStage0JsonHash` and Rust's bootstrap (`x.py`) already read
  the same local file.

The file is read without `git`, so this also works in source tarballs,
which have no `.git` directories.

This CL also removes the `rust_git_hash` parameter of
`FetchBetaPackage` and `InstallRustBetaSysroot`, because it is no
longer used.

constructor) and TabFeatures::WillDiscardContents.

parent
b8b4a414e3e631f8eff5da2b64382a46352d54f2 [ diff ] 
[DeviceAuth] Cancel pending key fetch when the primary account changes

Previously, the service kept pending callbacks in a map keyed by Gaia
ID, aiming to track fetches for different accounts independently. Doing
this correctly is tricky, as the access token must be requested, and the
fetched keys stored and returned, for the right account across primary
account switches. This adds complexity for a rare scenario that doesn't
need more than failing the request.

This CL simplifies the service to only ever fetch for the current
primary account, which is much easier to reason about:
* Concurrent requests are still merged: at most one fetch is in flight,
and all callers' callbacks are queued and receive its result
* If the primary account changes or is cleared while a fetch is pending,
the service cancels the fetch and fails the queued callbacks. The
returned errors are not granular yet; this is addressed in a separate CL

For this:
* DeviceAuthorizationKeysFetcher gets a Cancel() API that drops the
  in-flight EndpointFetcher without running its callback.
* DeviceAuthorizationServiceImpl observes IdentityManager and handles
  primary account changes and IdentityManager shutdown.
* Since only the current primary account can have a pending fetch,
  DeviceAuthorizationServiceImpl stores the Gaia ID of that fetch and a
  single vector of callbacks, instead of a map keyed by Gaia ID.

[iOS][PersistTabContext] Invalidate persisted tab contexts on navigation

Observe all realized WebStates in PersistTabContextBrowserAgent via
ScopedMultiSourceObservation and TabsDependencyInstaller so that
committed navigations in hidden tabs are observed.

1. Delete persisted tab contexts on any committed navigation in
   DidFinishNavigation.
2. Bind the WebState's last committed URL at extraction start and
   discard the extracted result in OnPageContextExtracted if the
   committed URL changed while extraction was in flight.
3. Validate fetched PageContext URLs against the live WebState's last
   committed URL in GetSingleContextAsync and GetMultipleContextsAsync,
   evicting stale entries and returning std::nullopt on mismatch.
4. Removed the OnPageLoad extraction timing param.

This fix actually caught the issue in a related unit test!
(os_smart_tab_grouping_request_wrapper_unittest)

[MagiChrome] Fix crash on inline QR code in password manual fallback

AppendOptionalFooterSection() adds the kWebauthnPasskeyQrCode
suggestion to the password manual fallback popup, but
PasswordManualFallbackFlow::SupportsSuggestionType() did not include
it. Selecting or accepting the QR code row therefore failed the CHECK
in DidSelectSuggestion() / DidAcceptSuggestion().

Support the type in PasswordManualFallbackFlow and handle it like
kWebauthnSignInWithAnotherDevice: selecting and accepting it are
forwarded to PasswordManagerDelegate::SelectSuggestion() and
AcceptSuggestion().

[Autofill] Move metrics recorder into AtMemoryPersistedStateManager

AtMemoryMetricsRecorder currently lives in AtMemoryManager::PopupState,
which ties a metrics session to a single popup instance. With search
statefulness the popup can be hidden and re-shown on the same field
while the search state (and any in-flight query) survives, so the
recorder has to outlive individual popups too.

Move metric recorder to AtMemoryPersistedStateManager and bind its
lifetime to the persisted search state:
* create when AtMemory is first shown on a field and reuse when the
  popup is re-shown on the same field,
* destroy whenever the persisted state is reset (focusing another
  field, accepting a suggestion, TTL expiry, history deletion,
  opt-out), which is when the session summary metrics are emitted,
* still hand over to the filling path when a suggestion is accepted.

As a result fix Autofill.AtMemory.QueryCompleted and the Latency.Query*
metrics. This is because OnQueryResponseReceived() is now also called
when a background query completes while the popup is closed.

This is the first step of the "Metrics implications" section of
go/at-mem-search-statefulness; the remaining action items (new
Autofill.AtMemory.StateRestored metric, re-recording SearchBarDisplayed
on every re-show, and the SuggestionFilled / SuggestionAccepted /
QueryCountBeforeAcceptance semantics changes) follow in separate CLs.

[SQLite Migration] Add PageMigrationTracker to sqlite_migration_vfs

Introduces components/sqlite_migration_vfs with PageMigrationTracker, an
in-memory tracker that monitors migration progress in 64-page blocks.

Key features:
- Tracks migration progress in contiguous 64-page blocks with per-block
locking to minimize thread contention.
- Uses a pre-allocated vector for O(1) block lookups and an atomic
counter for lock-free completion checks.
- Supports sequential background scanning via GetNextUnmigratedBlock().
- Includes unit tests in components_unittests and a component README.md.

BYPASS_LARGE_CHANGE_WARNING: This is part of migration tracker, needs to stay together.

[ash] Move speech_recognition_constants into //chromeos/ash

speech_recognition_constants.{h,cc} sat in chrome/browser/speech but is
ChromeOS-only, takes no Profile, and holds nothing but the
speech::SpeechRecognitionType enum and its conversion to the
speech_recognition_private extension API type.

Move it to //chromeos/ash/experiences/extensions/browser, so its nine
ash consumers depend on //chromeos rather than //chrome for it. That
directory is organised by process boundary and this is browser-process
only, so it creates browser/, which the README already anticipated. It
gets its own source_set so callers of a two-symbol leaf do not have to
pull in the extensions API provider.

This removes no DEPS rule: ash/extensions/speech and ash/accessibility
still include other chrome/browser/speech headers, so those allowances
stay.

#ai-assisted

[SendTabToSelf] Show submenus for desktop entry point sign-in promos

This CL adds the kSendTabToSelfSubmenuSigninPromos feature flag and
updates Send Tab to Self desktop menu entry points (tab context menu,
page and link context menus, and the Save and Share app menu) to display
a submenu with a sign-in promo when the flag is enabled.

When the user is signed out or requires reauthentication, the submenu
displays a "Not signed in" header and a "Sign in to Chrome" item with a
generic profile icon. When no target devices are available and
kSendTabToSelfNoTargetDeviceQrCode is also enabled, the submenu displays
a "No other device found" header and a "Sign in on your phone" item with
a phone icon. Clicking either item opens the corresponding Send Tab to
Self promo bubble.

No-devices submenu: https://screenshot.googleplex.com/BMDA6VrmuadNtyp

[ash] fileapi: take the permission context by constructor

FileChangeService took a Profile only to resolve the
ChromeFileSystemAccessPermissionContext it subscribes to, and did
nothing else with it. Take the permission context directly; its keyed
service factory, which already DependsOn() that context's factory, is
what resolves it from the profile.

The service no longer references Profile at all, and
file_change_service.cc no longer includes
chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h or the permission context's factory.
//chrome/browser/file_system_access is no longer a directory-wide
dependency of chrome/browser/ash/fileapi; what is left is scoped to the
three file_change_service files that use the context type itself.

#ai-assisted

[GEiC] Add purpose-keyed OpenAuthTab/CloseAuthTab for connector OAuth

The GEiC side panel is a privileged WebContents, so `window.open()` is
denied and 3P connector OAuth has to run in a browser tab. The GE client
currently opens that tab through glic's generic `createTab`, but has no
way to close it afterwards: script-initiated `window.close()` is blocked
for such tabs, so users are left on a "please close this tab" page.

Add a single `OpenAuthTab` / `CloseAuthTab` pair to
`GeminiEnterpriseHandler`, keyed by a fixed `AuthTabPurpose` enum
(`kSignIn`, `kConnectorOauth`):

* Each purpose has its own browser-side URL allowlist, its own tracked
  tab, and its own UMA (`Geic.AuthTab.{Open,Close}Result.{Purpose}`).
* `kConnectorOauth` only accepts the GE OAuth redirector
  (`/oauth-redirect` on the default redirector origin
  `vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com` or the guest origin); the 3P
  provider in `continue_uri` is intentionally not validated. A reused
  OAuth tab is navigated, since each flow has a fresh `state`.
* A tracked tab is only reused or closed while it is still on an origin
  expected for its purpose; if the user navigates it elsewhere, it is
  left open (`CloseAuthTabResult::kNavigatedAway`). `CloseAuthTab` can
  only close the tab Chrome opened for that purpose, and restores focus
  to the previously active tab only if the closed tab was still active.
  There is no generic close-arbitrary-tab capability.
* Unknown purposes (e.g. from a newer client via the [Extensible]
  default) are rejected.

The open/track/close/restore-focus logic moves from
`GlicGeminiEnterpriseManager` into a new `GeicManagedTab` helper.
`OpenSignInTab` / `CloseSignInTab` are kept as deprecated aliases for
`kSignIn` so existing clients keep working. The TS methods are optional
on `GeicBrowserHost` so the client can feature-detect them.

[APC] Enforce runtime host policy across experimentalAiData

getAiData and getAiDataWithSpecifier currently collect page data without
checking the calling extension's runtime blocked hosts. Check the target
page, its frames and embedded contents, and other tabs requested by the
collection options. Honor runtime allowed-host exceptions.

This is in preparation for CL 8343087, which adds APC capability to
experimentalAIData. The APC capability needed to check runtime blocked
hosts, and it became clear that this was missing from the original
experimentalAiData.

[iOS][Cobrowse] Validate tab extractability and exclude ineligible URLs

If an auto-added tab fails context extraction in the background, showing
an error snackbar interrupts the user without explicit intent.

This CL resolves this by:
- Checking CanExtractPageContextForWebState before attaching active tabs.
- Suppressing failure snackbars for auto-added items so implicit
  background failures fail silently.
